It can be found that the introduction of NaFSI into the single-salt system improves the battery capacity retention rate and recovery rate by 14.1%/11.6% (7D) and 4.8%/6.4% (14D), respectively. The huge improvement in calendar aging performance shows that the self-discharge of the NNFM111/HC full cell during the storage at $60^{\circ}$ C is suppressed, and the internal side reactions are reduced. A large amount of gas fills in the battery makes the contact between the materials worse, which ultimately leads to an increase in the impedance of the battery and a drastic decrease in the capacity retention rate. At the same time, the production of a large amount of gas also means that the side reaction inside the battery is very serious, and a large amount of electrolyte components decompose to produce gas.
